Moreinfo: Hey!
Great to see you at my profile.

I'm coming from a systems/networking background, working as a classic system administrator for the first year of my career, then gradually switching towards infra engineering and clouds, the stuff I've been working with ever since.

So, what do I bring to the table?
Deep Linux and networking knowledge, hands-on experience with AWS, all the stuff related to web operations, monitoring&logging. I also can write code in python/php though I'm not a programmer by trade.
On a personal side: down to earth person who is willing to help, proactive and patient. I've worked in both distributed and local office teams.
But enough about me.
What do I expect from you ? 
0) No legacy. Or at least there is a planned migration. PHP5.6 on Ubuntu 14.04 doesn't sound sexy at all.

Position: Blockchain Analyst
Moreinfo: As an Investment Analyst at a blockchain-focused investment fund, my responsibilities included:

1. Research and analysis: I conducted thorough research and analysis on blockchain-related startups and investment opportunities. This involved reviewing pitch decks, whitepapers, and other relevant documents to evaluate the potential of the project, the team behind it, the market opportunity, and other key factors.
2. Due diligence: I ensured that potential investments aligned with the fund's investment strategy and risk profile by conducting financial analysis, market research, and risk assessment.
3. Reporting: I provided regular reports to the board of directors to update them on the fund's performance, investment pipeline, and other key metrics. I analyzed data and presented findings in a clear and concise manner.
4. Portfolio management: I managed the fund's investments, including monitoring the performance of existing investments and making recommendations for new investments or divestitures.
5. Relationship management: I built and maintained relationships with portfolio companies, industry contacts, and other stakeholders in the blockchain ecosystem.
6. Industry research: I stayed up-to-date with developments in the blockchain industry, including trends, new technologies, and regulatory changes, and assessed their potential impact on the fund's investment strategy.
7. Team collaboration: I shared insights and ideas with other members of the investment team, and contributed to the overall success of the fund.

In addition to these responsibilities, I also found new investment opportunities, negotiated deal terms, and participated in industry events and conferences. I am proud of my accomplishments and successes, including successful rounds of investment in prominent blockchain startups and a low acceptance rate, which demonstrated my value as an Investment Analyst.

I believe that by developing a deeper understanding of these topics, I can make more informed investment decisions and provide greater value to the fund and its stakeholders. Additionally, I am excited about the potential for blockchain technology to drive innovation and create new opportunities across industries, and I am eager to contribute to this movement by advancing my knowledge and expertise in these areas.

Position: AI Team Lead / ML Engineer / Data Engineer
Moreinfo: The main part of my IT career was in France. After some Java internship, got my first Data Science job in 2015. Then, in 2017-2020, had several Data Science/Data Engineering jobs, covering a wide range of tasks: from research/prototyping to data engineering and devops activities for deploying ML models. 

In 2021-2022 I had a role of AI Team Lead, delivering various AI applications to the clients, with hands-on experience as well as team and people management activities.

Originally from Ukraine, i lived in Paris in 2011-2019 and in Berlin in 2019-2020. This gave me a good experience in working with European clients and a lot of foreign languages practice (especially English and French). In 2021 i moved back to Ukraine.

I also like teaching: in 2018-19 gave several 1-week introductory courses on Machine Learning / Deep Learning to the students of Pierre-Marie Curie university in Paris.

Interested in designing/building/deploying Machine Learning systems. A mix of a solid mathematical background (theoretical physics MSc in Ukraine and France) and a software engineering education make me relevant for a wide range of Data Science/Machine Learning/Deep Learning positions, from prototyping ideas to deploying models in production.

Want to be a part of a strong Machine Learning/Data Engineering team, being able to constantly learn and grow. 

Most interested in domains like computer vision, medical, transport, "social good", ecology. Less interested in marketing, retail.

Social aspect is very important to me: knowing that the results of my work help to improve people's lives.

Agile methodology is preferred, with very clear communication. 

In case of an international collaboration, the company could also benefit from my knowledge of foreign languages and almost 10 years of observing the culture/mentality of Western Europe.

Deployed an image classification system, based on satellite images (100 megapixel, 1 meter resolution) from Sentinel satellite of EU Copernicus program. System is used for ice segmentation in the Arctic Ocean, improving safety of ships navigation.

Was teaching 4 introductory 1-week courses on Machine Learning / Deep Learning to the students of Pierre-Marie Curie university in Paris.

In a team of 4, built a hackathon winning Flask/Leaflet web application: animation of map-matched trajectories on the transport network of France.

Built a centralized system for storing all marketing costs (25 channels/vendors) of a NYSE public company. Reports based on this data are more stable, allowing Business Intelligence, Strategy, Marketing teams to plan marketing campaigns more accurately.

Participated in French Robotics Cup 2016.

Position: Academic Writer
Moreinfo: I am a software engineer moving from academic research to the software development industry. For the past 10 years I have been developing and studying tools working with software specifications on different levels, be it business requirements, software documentation, or formal specifications (contracts, assertions, you name it) for software verification and testing. 

As a part of my research I've worked on tool support for behavior-driven development. The goal of the project was to provide a low-code solution to write Gherkin scenarios so that non-technical stakeholders can participate in product behavior specification and review directly. My team has also studied how our tool solution would improve the traceability between requirements and the actual implementation code within the SDLC, and we have published two articles on the topic.

I have also enjoyed working pro bono as a technical business analyst with a Dnipro-based cultural space in 2020, who were interested in expanding their web presence. I took on the tasks of requirements collection and analysis, communicating closely with both the cultural space representatives and the technical team of development volunteers from the first brainstorming meeting till the website launch. 

Apart from requirements engineering I also worked on software analysis directly. I have worked on several projects using NLP to detect documentation inconsistent with the source code. Prior to that I have been working on scatic code analyses for software verification, optimizing the executable checks of formal program specifications.

Overall, as a software engineer I have used different tools and technologies over the years. I did enjoy 3+ years with C++ and Java each, and I have 5+ years of Prolog experience. I have been extending software verification frameworks and buildings standalone tools for program analyses. As a researcher, I used LaTeX as my main tool for document preparation and generation, so any kind of markup is familiar to me. To manage my own work and coordinate with my team members I rely on different tools, from Trello and Notion to Google Docs. For more development-oriented management I rely on GitLab and Phabricator.  For the last 2 years I have also been managing international distributed teams, typically of size 4-6 people.

Currently, I am looking for opportunities to join a team working on their own product.

Due to the russian invasion into Ukraine, I am currently based in Switzerland.
Highlights: 2.5 years ago I have changed the domain in which I work, and in this time I have:
- moved from working mostly in one small team of 3 people to managing 5 teams, all of it remotely due to the corona pandemic. We still published 5 papers, 3 of them in top venues in the fields;
- established two international project collaborations between different research institutions, and kept them going;
- taught classes on algorithms and data structures, both online and in-person, including lecture material development from scratch and recording it as video lectures.

Since the beginning of the russian invasion into Ukraine I am volunteering actively. In the first chaotic week of the war I have managed to organize equipment delivery over two state borders, including fundraising. I had zero previos experience in logistics. But it was a problem to solve, and I like both problem solving and getting things done.
